description:
Scope: Test-only coverage for lib/zaq/engine/messages/incoming/audience.ex:48,53. No production behavior/API changes. Exclusive edit path: test/zaq/engine/messages/incoming/audience_test.exs. Do not edit any other test file, production module, fixture, support module, or configuration. Existing test module uses ExUnit.Case async: true and already covers 150 valid recipients and 101 out-of-audience participant entries followed by valid metadata; extend it rather than duplicate those cases. The module's @moduledoc describes untrusted data normalized from trusted Channels evidence; tests call Audience.normalize/1 directly, not transport or BO/router paths. Action reuse gate: not applicable, no executable operation, Action, tool, or workflow change; reuse Audience.normalize/1 and the existing unit test module.

Test-first scenarios and exact assertions:
1. Line 48 catch-all inside Enum.flat_map/2: with valid top-level platform: "email", sender: "sender@example.com", recipients: ["recipient@example.com"], and a participants list containing a valid sender entry, malformed entries such as nil, "unexpected", %{identifier: "recipient@example.com"} (missing role), %{identifier: "recipient@example.com", role: :bcc} (unsupported role), %{identifier: "recipient@example.com", role: "to"} (wrong role type), and a valid recipient entry at the end, assert %Audience{}, exact audience.participants == [%{identifier: "sender@example.com", role: :sender, display_name: nil}, %{identifier: "recipient@example.com", role: :cc, display_name: "Recipient"}]. Assert sender, platform and recipients unchanged. This forces the catch-all for non-map and malformed maps and proves later valid evidence survives without promoting unknown roles or inventing identities; avoid duplicating existing outsider-ID rejection test. Include a tuple or atom only if it improves the contract without adding redundant assertions. The first valid entry missing display_name also confirms the documented nil default, not a change to normalization.
2. Line 53 non-list fallback: use a valid top-level audience and participants: %{identifier: "recipient@example.com", role: :to, display_name: "Recipient"} (valid-looking map but not a list); assert normalized %Audience{}, exact participants == [], and exact unchanged platform/sender/recipients. Add a separate nil participants case (or one small table of map, nil, scalar) asserting the same output if helpful to prove the optional malformed field does not reject otherwise valid evidence. A missing participants key already goes through the default [] clause; do not confuse that path with line 53. Never expect malformed top-level recipients to reach this fallback: the is_list(recipients) guard prevents it.
3. Property assessment: normalization/filtering accepts broad lists and enforces a safety default, so add one focused bounded ExUnitProperties/StreamData property in this same file (existing project dependency and pattern: test/zaq/engine/messages/incoming_identifier_property_test.exs). Generate bounded lists (0..20) of known-valid sender/recipient metadata and known-invalid elements (missing/unsupported/string role, non-map, outsider identifier); fixed valid platform/sender/recipients. For each generated list, compute expected sequence by filtering only entries matching %{identifier: id, role: role} with role in [:sender, :to, :cc] and id in [sender | recipients], then projecting identifier/role/display_name via Map.get; assert exact participants equality and normalized top-level fields. Avoid computing expected via Audience internals or replicating a second complex implementation; use simple declarative expected filter/projection. If property construction would obscure the two concrete regression tests, retain two examples and explicitly record why the property is omitted; it must not replace them. Domain constrain generators, not arbitrary garbage, and use small bounded run count if needed.

Fixtures/helpers/mocks/isolation: inline minimal literal maps and optional local test helper for the repeated valid base attrs only if it improves clarity; reuse existing alias and test module. No DB, factory, shared fixture, Mox, process, network, clock, sleep, application env, global state, sandbox, or NodeRouter involved. Keep async: true; no async: false module or mocks required. Assertions target observable return struct and exact participant order/content, not private helper calls. No extra dependency or production test seam needed.

Validation for implementing agent (not executed in this planning issue): run isolated `mix test test/zaq/engine/messages/incoming/audience_test.exs` via Context Mode, then `mix q` via Context Mode (includes format); inspect diff for exclusive test path, do not weaken existing assertions; rerun fresh coverage report only within the authorized coverage phase (mix coveralls.json then mix coverup per workflow) and verify both source lines 48 and 53 are hit. Final mix precommit belongs to the final approval gate, not this plan. This is unit-only regression work; no new feature UX/E2E and no human UX gate is triggered.

Reachability/blockers: Both lines are directly reachable through the public normalize/1 with valid top-level fields, so no unreachable-code blocker or production edits are expected. If fresh coverage still reports either line missed after these tests, confirm report freshness/source version and inspect branch line attribution before proposing changes; do not claim coverage based on green tests alone. If dependency/runtime prevents validation, report the exact blocker and leave the issue open; do not silently alter production code or shared setup.
